title: Finite projective-line comparison isomorphism
statement: theorem finiteP1_kummer_comparison_iso {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian S] (e : X ≅ ProjectiveLine S) (cX : Chern l E X) (hS : IsUnit (l : Γ(S, ⊤))) (n : ℕ) [Finite (SpTowerShriek.R l E n)] {hX : IsUnit ((l ^ (n + 1) : ℕ) : Γ(X, ⊤))} (c : SpTowerP1.CoefficientCoordinates l E n X hX) : ∃ t : (SpTowerShriek.Ev l E X n).obj ((line l E cX)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧) ≅ (finiteOverRealization l E n e).obj (geoP1Twist (FiniteRing l E n) (l ^ (n + 1)) (ULift.ext _ _ (coefficient_annihilates l E n)) (ProjectiveLine S) 1 2)

source.place: paragraph (1), finite coefficient comparison before the system splitting

proof.text: Apply nuSingle, the derived single functor to c.line and the inverse of lineEvaluation, and the inverse exact-evaluation single comparison. Shift this composite by 2 and compose with the canonical commShiftIso comparisons. This gives an isomorphism from nu of the ordinary shifted finite Tate line on X to Ev of the shifted tower line. The positive signed twist is definitionally that ordinary shifted line.

The unit hS remains a unit after taking its (n+1)-st power and pulling it to ProjectiveLine S. Apply geoP1TwistPullback along e.hom to the positive twist and shift 2. Map its inverse through the intrinsic derived realization functor. Compose this with the inverse of the first isomorphism and introduce Nonempty. All isomorphisms are explicit; no Chern arrow, decomposition, or cohomology theorem is used.

proof_origin.place: paragraph (1), line identification; explicit composition of existing normalized coefficient, single, shift, and twist-pullback isomorphisms (G6)
